title: Wagertech <> Jumpr: Redeposits Discovery Part 2

items.topic: Monthly budget by deal entered manually
items.statement: WagerTech does not want to automate the budget setting by deal yet. The budget is a field or input that WagerTech enters, and then the allocation process starts from that budget. Jumpr agreed.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: I think the first piece, like you just said, is the budget. budget setting by deal and I don't think we're at a point to be able to automate that piece where it's like we where we understand exactly the correct amount to like start with and then splice out. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Mhm. / Joyce Kiddell: So if to start if we can just like solution for being like a field or like something that we can input ourselves um and then Alli's process will take over. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yes. / Emily Vandenberg: Yep.

items.topic: Allocation targets signup month per book
items.statement: Budget notes such as 'all from July' mean redeposits for that book go to new players who registered and played on that book in that month; priority is newer clients, older clients may get them if budget allows.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: when it says like all from July, um, does that mean we're targeting, uh, players that signed up for Bet MGM in July? / Ali Nawaz: Exactly. Yes. / Ali Nawaz: so no, exactly. It would have to be the new players who registered and played in July.

items.statement: Assigned redeposit slots currently stay in a $30 to $80 range (average about $40). The slots are added to BA sheets with no player name, and the BA decides which client gets each slot.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: right now we kind of stick in a range of $30 to $80 when it comes to the readups that we offer. So 30 35 40 45 right and they're just all added to the BA sheets with no names beside them obviously and that's when the BA decides which clients he's going to offer them to.

items.topic: Payment tracker tool does initial allocation
items.statement: A standalone tool built by Jay (the 'payment tracker' site) does the initial volume-based allocation of assigned redeposits. Ali then makes manual adjustments per BA. Ali has used it for two months and says it works well and saves time.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: It's Emily. It's the um payment tracker site. / Ali Nawaz: The payment tracker. Exactly. It is. Yeah, / Ali Nawaz: So, for me, this this works. If you guys want to make any changes that you could definitely do that, but Jay was the one who created this. He worked with me to figure out what what we need. Uh, like I said, regardless, there's still a lot of manual touches that I have to do at the end, but this helps save a lot of time for sure.

items.statement: Emily said WagerTech needs to understand product ownership of the payment tracker tool and take that offline.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: Lina,what I don't know is like who actually is doing the I think we have to take that offline, but I think we need to understand kind of product ownership on this tool a bit more. / Lina Ceniccola: on the this redeposit tool. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah. Like what we're calling the payment tracker in general.

items.statement: Lina will follow up to get the payment tracker tool renamed to avoid confusion.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: Oh yeah, I've asked him to update this name a couple times just to avoid confusion. So, let me uh follow up on that. What?

items.statement: Ali offered to get Jay (tool builder) on a call, or to relay questions to Jay, about how the tool works on the back end. No meeting was confirmed as a next step.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: Like the best thing is for me to get Jay to join and you could speak to him about any of that because I I / Ali Nawaz: If you guys need to get another call, just let me know. And like I said, when it comes to that payment tracker or that that she sorry, that website, uh I could always find out any questions you have for for you from Jay or he could get on call with us.

items.topic: Keep allocation logic in tool for V1
items.statement: For V1 the allocation tool is not replaced: Salesforce replaces the spreadsheets and feeds the raw signup data, and the logic that breaks budgets into assignments stays in the tool. Ali agreed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: right. Okay. So, like we don't need to I don't I don't think we need to replace this tool, but I think we can connect Salesforce to it in a way where Salesforce is able to feed those signups from uh because like ultimately that's where we're going to start tracking it, right? And there's going to be like all the gating and everything and all the logic that's going to happen. / Ali Nawaz: Of course. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So it should replace the spreadsheets. So Salesforce could feed the raw like the signup data that uh we get from it. Um the logic of breaking down the uh assignments based on the V deposits could be done uh through this tool like for V1

items.statement: Moving the allocation logic into Salesforce is a later discussion, not V1.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: like for V1 and we can talk about like whether we want to absorb this into Salesforce later.

items.topic: CSV export uploaded to Salesforce for V1
items.statement: Kobi proposed that, maybe for V1, the tool output is exported as a CSV and uploaded into Salesforce, which creates the allocation records under the deal; reassignment and tracking then happen in Salesforce. Ali said it would help. Later Kobi left open whether the tool spins out a CSV or talks directly to Salesforce.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. So this is where I think Salesforce can take over where you don't have to do it in / Ali Nawaz: that would help. Yeah, for sure. / Kobi Kunasekaran: spreadsheets anymore like the maybe for V1 like we still have uh the the path / Ali Nawaz: Yeah. / Kobi Kunasekaran: of like you export the CSV here but you upload it into Salesforce and Salesforce creates the respective records under the deal and then you can reassign do everything that you do in spreadsheets but you do it in Salesforce and then we're we're able to also do the tracking and everything in Salesforce.

items.topic: Future direct upload button to Salesforce
items.statement: In a future version the tool could have an 'upload to Salesforce' button, integrated like the CMS DRA upload, to remove the download/upload step.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh but in a future future version we could have a button that just says upload to Salesforce. um and just have this integrated similar to like the CMS DRA upload um where you don't / Ali Nawaz: Yeah. items.statement: WagerTech needs the ability to create manual redeposit records (manual overrides, extra allocations) for edge cases. Kobi confirmed Salesforce gives this through the interface discussed last week, where additional redeposit allocations can be added in bulk to deals and people.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: so, as long as we have the ability to also create manual redeposit records, that's really important. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. I mean that that's what Salesforce is going to give you, right? like you do have the ability to um like the interface that we talked about last week um where you can add additional uh additional allocations for redeposits in bulk to deals to people.

items.topic: Feed Salesforce manual additions back to tool
items.statement: Open: how manual/additional redeposits added in Salesforce get back into the allocation tool so the next month's run factors those decisions.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: and then we we'll have to figure out how we can get that back into this tool in case you know you're adding a new Ruby deposit and you need to factor those previous decisions for the next month. So we'll have to kind of figure that out.

items.statement: There can be several batches of assigned redeposits for the same book in the same month, plus manually added edge-case redeposits. Kobi said adding manual allocations is fine.

I'm not concerned.

items.quote: Ali Nawaz: But then is it would be good to have like some kind of historical data on when it was added and the the total budget additional budget they were assigned.

items.statement: Reporting on redeposit progress (percent complete, player lists) will be part of the solution once redeposits are allocated to the right player.

Kind of once everything's like flowing through, then we could easily and like as long as it's like being allocated to the right player, like we set up the right infrastructure, then yes, like we'll be able to take and report off of, you know, the uh percent complete and even like more easily kind of like player lists, etc.

items.statement: Requests for additional assigned redeposits come through Jay and Owen to Ali; Ali requests budget he does not have from Ilas. Unassigned redeposits left from a month's budget can be offered out during the month. No system approval process was decided.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: Ali,you're the only one who can like approve manually assigned readups. Is that correct? / Ali Nawaz: Uh Jay Jay kind of goes and works with me with and Owen as well when they when they have somebody who needs it, they would request it. But it's not obviously like I make the decision if I just feel like it goes by whatever is available. And that's where uh sometimes there let's just say somebody we were assigned total 500 and I need to assign a few more like that's where in the past I had to reach out to Jess about it and now I I reach out to Ilas. So ILAS is kind of the person who uh I request any budgets that I can't I don't have any volume for you know if I let's say we had 500 reads the previous month, but I only gave out 460. I still have 40, which means that I could offer those out at any time throughout the month, you know.

items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: So you might want to like even have an option to uh cancel what was assigned like the rest. / Lina Ceniccola: So you have all these and then you could see like all these redeposits are open for the month. you might just want to go end all like we've we've overspent

items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: And it'd be great to be able to see like in live time how the payments are / Lina Ceniccola: actually flowing with each book and that will help us make better decisions on like okay this we actually don't have additional redeposit budget on draft king CTM. So you might want to like even have an option to uh cancel what was assigned like the rest.

items.topic: No hard guard rails on amounts
items.statement: Kobi asked whether to add thresholds or hard limits (e.g. alert above $125, no single redeposit above $80). Lina chose to leave it open and adjust later based on data.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: I think I lean more towards leave it open and / Ali Nawaz: Yeah. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. / Lina Ceniccola: adjust later and see how it goes. Like we have people to manage the system. So I'm not overly concerned about people going rogue or anything like that. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. / Lina Ceniccola: Let's leave it open and adjust later.

But let's let's not allow BAS to change the assigned / Kobi Kunasekaran: Perfect. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I mean with Salesforce like we can do hard lots right

items.statement: If a BA needs an amount outside the assigned slots, it is always additional budget and must be approved first.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: but if they need to add an amount, it should it's always an additional budget and it has to be approved in the first place

And uh I think that's all from that side.
